claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 3F-G.

claims.claim: The PE composition defects in paqr-2(tm3410) mutant are partially corrected by mdt-15(et14) or fld-1(et48) mutations, and fully corrected by a combination of both mutations.
claims.source: An analysis of the PE composition in worms challenged with growth on glucose shows that the paqr-2(tm3410) mutant has an excess of SFAs and reduced levels of LCPUFAs, and that these defects are partially corrected by the mdt-15(et14) or fld-1(et48) mutations, and fully corrected by a combination of both these mutations (Figure 3F–G).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 3F-G.

claims.claim: The levels of monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs) were unchanged in the PEs of the fld-1 mutant, even in combination with the mdt-15(et14) mutation.
claims.source: The levels of monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs) were unchanged in the PEs of the fld-1 mutant, even in combination with the mdt-15(et14) mutation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Cholesterol does not appear to play a structural role in C. elegans but instead is a likely precursor for essential low-abundance metabolites.
claims.source: Note that the lipidomic analysis was performed on whole worms, and thus reflects global lipid composition rather than the composition of any specific membrane; also, cholesterol levels were not measured since this lipid does not appear to play a structural role in C. elegans but instead is a likely precursor for essential low-abundance metabolites (Merris et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Merris et al., 2004.

claims.claim: fld-1(et48) and mdt-15(et14) mutations do not cause excess membrane fluidity either by themselves or in combination.
claims.source: Some mechanism likely exists to prevent excess membrane fluidity since the fld-1(et48) and mdt-15(et14) mutations do not cause an excess fluidity either by themselves or in combination in any of the tested conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Some mechanism likely exists to prevent excess membrane fluidity.
claims.source: Some mechanism likely exists to prevent excess membrane fluidity since the fld-1(et48) and mdt-15(et14) mutations do not cause an excess fluidity either by themselves or in combination in any of the tested conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that fld-1 and mdt-15 mutations do not cause excess fluidity.

claims.claim: The fld-1 mutation suppresses the growth defect of the fat-2 mutant both on normal plates and plates containing 20 mM glucose.
claims.source: We found that, indeed, the fld-1 mutation suppresses the growth defect of the fat-2 mutant both on normal plates and plates containing 20 mM glucose, even in a paqr-2(tm3410) mutant background (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by growth assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A-C.

claims.claim: The fld-1 mutation causes either increased production of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids or lowers their turnover.
claims.source: We interpret these results to mean that the fld-1 mutation causes either increased production of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids or lowers their turnover; either effect therefore allows the abundance of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids to reach an increased level in membranes even if their production is reduced by mutations in paqr-2, iglr-2 or fat-2.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the genetic interaction data.

claims.claim: fld-1(et48) can suppress the inability of the paqr-2 mutant to accumulate exogenously provided EPA.
claims.source: This interpretation is further supported by the observation that fld-1(et48) can suppress the inability of the paqr-2 mutant to accumulate the exogenously provided LCPUFAs eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; 20:5) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D); notably, this demonstrates that no synthesis of LCPUFAs is required for fld-1(et48) to promote their accumulation among phospholipids.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claims.claim: No synthesis of LCPUFAs is required for fld-1(et48) to promote their accumulation among phospholipids.
claims.source: This interpretation is further supported by the observation that fld-1(et48) can suppress the inability of the paqr-2 mutant to accumulate the exogenously provided LCPUFAs eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; 20:5) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D); notably, this demonstrates that no synthesis of LCPUFAs is required for fld-1(et48) to promote their accumulation among phospholipids.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the EPA supplementation experiment.

claims.claim: TLCD1 is most strongly expressed in heart, muscle, liver and fat in mouse.
claims.source: The mouse and human TLCD1 and TLCD2 genes are expressed in a variety of tissues, with heart, muscle, liver and fat being strongest for TLCD1 and heart, muscle, liver, small intestine and fat being strongest for the more variably expressed TLCD2 (Fagerberg et al., 2014) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fagerberg et al., 2014 and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: TLCD2 is most strongly expressed in heart, muscle, liver, small intestine and fat in mouse.
claims.source: The mouse and human TLCD1 and TLCD2 genes are expressed in a variety of tissues, with heart, muscle, liver and fat being strongest for TLCD1 and heart, muscle, liver, small intestine and fat being strongest for the more variably expressed TLCD2 (Fagerberg et al., 2014) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fagerberg et al., 2014 and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Knockdown of TLCD1 or TLCD2 using siRNA in human HEK293 cells has little effect under normal conditions.
claims.source: The molecular function of these proteins in mammals appears conserved with that of the C. elegans fld-1: knockdown of either gene using siRNA in human HEK293 cells has little effect on these cells under normal conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–D) but was protective against the membrane rigidifying effects of PA (Figure 4A–B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2E); knockdown of the control gene PPIB had no effect on membrane fluidity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F–G).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-D.

claims.claim: Knockdown of TLCD1 or TLCD2 was protective against the membrane rigidifying effects of PA in HEK293 cells.
claims.source: The molecular function of these proteins in mammals appears conserved with that of the C. elegans fld-1: knockdown of either gene using siRNA in human HEK293 cells has little effect on these cells under normal conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–D) but was protective against the membrane rigidifying effects of PA (Figure 4A–B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2E); knockdown of the control gene PPIB had no effect on membrane fluidity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F–G).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 4A-B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: Knockdown of TLCD1 or TLCD2 protected HEK293 cells from PA-induced apoptosis.
claims.source: Importantly, knockdown of TLCD1 and TLCD2 also protected the HEK293 cells from PA-induced apoptosis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H–I).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by apoptosis assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2H-I.

claims.claim: TLCD1 and TLCD2 do not regulate the uptake of exogenous SFAs.
claims.source: TLCD1 and TLCD2 do not regulate the uptake of exogenous SFAs since there is no difference in the uptake rate of labelled PA in HEK293 cells treated with siRNA against either gene (Figure 4—figure supplement 2J).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by PA uptake assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2J.

claims.claim: The SFA content in the TAGs of PA-treated HEK293 cells is unaffected by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown.
claims.source: The SFA content in the TAGs of PA-treated HEK293 cells is also unaffected by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 2K), as is their TAG/PC ratio (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L) and Nile red staining of lipid stores (Figure 4—figure supplement 2M–N), suggesting no effect on either uptake or sequestering of FAs.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2K.

claims.claim: TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown does not affect TAG/PC ratio in PA-treated HEK293 cells.
claims.source: The SFA content in the TAGs of PA-treated HEK293 cells is also unaffected by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 2K), as is their TAG/PC ratio (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L) and Nile red staining of lipid stores (Figure 4—figure supplement 2M–N), suggesting no effect on either uptake or sequestering of FAs.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2L.

claims.claim: TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown does not affect Nile red staining of lipid stores in PA-treated HEK293 cells.
claims.source: The SFA content in the TAGs of PA-treated HEK293 cells is also unaffected by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 2K), as is their TAG/PC ratio (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L) and Nile red staining of lipid stores (Figure 4—figure supplement 2M–N), suggesting no effect on either uptake or sequestering of FAs.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Nile red staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2M-N.

claims.claim: TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown does not affect uptake or sequestering of FAs.
claims.source: The SFA content in the TAGs of PA-treated HEK293 cells is also unaffected by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 2K), as is their TAG/PC ratio (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L) and Nile red staining of lipid stores (Figure 4—figure supplement 2M–N), suggesting no effect on either uptake or sequestering of FAs.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of changes in TAG content and lipid stores.

claims.claim: The expression levels of the desaturases SCD and FADS1-3 are not increased by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown.
claims.source: The expression levels of the desaturases SCD and FADS1-3 are also not increased by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 2O) ruling this out as a mechanism for the fluidizing effect; indeed, the SCD expression is downregulated in TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown which may reflect a decreased demand on their activity.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2O.

claims.claim: SCD expression is downregulated in TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown.
claims.source: The expression levels of the desaturases SCD and FADS1-3 are also not increased by TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 2O) ruling this out as a mechanism for the fluidizing effect; indeed, the SCD expression is downregulated in TLCD1 or TLCD2 knockdown which may reflect a decreased demand on their activity.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2O.

claims.claim: TLCD1 knockdown causes a marked increase in the abundance of 18:2, 20:5 and 22:6 LCPUFAs in the PEs.
claims.source: This conclusion is supported by the marked increase in the abundance of the 18:2, 20:5 and 22:6 LCPUFAs in the PEs of TLCD1 knockdown cells, and of the 18:2, 18:3 and 20:5 LCPUFAs in the PCs of TLCD2 knockdown cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: TLCD2 knockdown causes an increase in the abundance of 18:2, 18:3 and 20:5 LCPUFAs in the PCs.
claims.source: This conclusion is supported by the marked increase in the abundance of the 18:2, 20:5 and 22:6 LCPUFAs in the PEs of TLCD1 knockdown cells, and of the 18:2, 18:3 and 20:5 LCPUFAs in the PCs of TLCD2 knockdown cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Cultivating HEK293 cells in the presence of exogenous EPA leads to its excess accumulation in PCs and PEs when TLCD2 is knocked down.
claims.source: Cultivating HEK293 cells in the presence of exogenous EPA leads to its excess accumulation in PCs and PEs when TLCD2 is knocked down (Figure 4D–E), which demonstrates that, as in C. elegans, de novo PUFA synthesis is not required for the TLCD2 effect on PUFA-containing phospholipids; no change in TAG storage or EPA storage in TAGs occurred upon TLCD2 knockdown, indicating that TLCD2 does not regulate fatty acid storage or LCPUFA uptake (Figure 4—figure supplement 3I–J).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4D-E.

claims.claim: De novo PUFA synthesis is not required for the TLCD2 effect on PUFA-containing phospholipids.
claims.source: Cultivating HEK293 cells in the presence of exogenous EPA leads to its excess accumulation in PCs and PEs when TLCD2 is knocked down (Figure 4D–E), which demonstrates that, as in C. elegans, de novo PUFA synthesis is not required for the TLCD2 effect on PUFA-containing phospholipids; no change in TAG storage or EPA storage in TAGs occurred upon TLCD2 knockdown, indicating that TLCD2 does not regulate fatty acid storage or LCPUFA uptake (Figure 4—figure supplement 3I–J).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the EPA supplementation experiment.

claims.claim: TLCD2 does not regulate fatty acid storage or LCPUFA uptake.
claims.source: Cultivating HEK293 cells in the presence of exogenous EPA leads to its excess accumulation in PCs and PEs when TLCD2 is knocked down (Figure 4D–E), which demonstrates that, as in C. elegans, de novo PUFA synthesis is not required for the TLCD2 effect on PUFA-containing phospholipids; no change in TAG storage or EPA storage in TAGs occurred upon TLCD2 knockdown, indicating that TLCD2 does not regulate fatty acid storage or LCPUFA uptake (Figure 4—figure supplement 3I–J).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3I-J.

claims.claim: As little as 1 μM of EPA or DHA prevents membrane rigidification by 400 μM PA in HEK293 cells.
claims.source: The effect of TLCD2 knockdown on phospholipid EPA levels is especially interesting since LCPUFAs are very potent fluidizing lipids (Yang et al., 2011), which we confirmed experimentally in our cell system where as little as 1 μM of EPA or docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) prevents membrane rigidification by 400 μM PA (Figure 4F–G).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: LCPUFAs are very potent fluidizing lipids.
claims.source: The effect of TLCD2 knockdown on phospholipid EPA levels is especially interesting since LCPUFAs are very potent fluidizing lipids (Yang et al., 2011), which we confirmed experimentally in our cell system where as little as 1 μM of EPA or docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) prevents membrane rigidification by 400 μM PA (Figure 4F–G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2011 and confirmed by experimental data in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: TLCD2 knockdown caused increased incorporation of LA in PCs and PEs within 6 hr of incubation.
claims.source: The results show that TLCD2 knockdown caused increased incorporation of LA in PCs and PEs within 6 hr of incubation, and that increased incorporation was also evident by 24 hr in the PEs of TLCD1 and TLCD2 knockdown cells (Figure 4H–I).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by 13C-labeled LA incorporation experiments shown in Figure 4H-I.

claims.claim: Increased LA incorporation was evident by 24 hr in the PEs of TLCD1 and TLCD2 knockdown cells.
claims.source: The results show that TLCD2 knockdown caused increased incorporation of LA in PCs and PEs within 6 hr of incubation, and that increased incorporation was also evident by 24 hr in the PEs of TLCD1 and TLCD2 knockdown cells (Figure 4H–I).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by 13C-labeled LA incorporation experiments shown in Figure 4H-I.

claims.claim: No obvious differences were observed in TLCD1/2 knockdown cells during the chase part of the LA incorporation experiment.
claims.source: No obvious differences were observed in the TLCD1/2 knockdown cells during the chase part of the experiment (Figure 4—figure supplement 3K–L).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the chase experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3K-L.

claims.claim: The primary function of TLCD1 and TLCD2 is to limit the formation of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids rather than promote their turnover.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that the primary function of TLCD1 and TLCD2 is to limit the formation of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids rather than promote their turnover.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the increased incorporation but no change in turnover of labeled LA.

claims.claim: TLCD2 siRNA protects against the potentiated rigidifying effects of PA when the FADS2 desaturase is knocked down.
claims.source: Firstly, we found that TLCD2 siRNA protects against the potentiated rigidifying effects of PA when the FADS2 desaturase is knocked down (Figure 4J–K; Figure 4—figure supplement 3M), just as the fld-1 mutation suppressed the effects of the fat-2 mutation in C. elegans; this also strengthens the conclusion that TLCD2 acts independently from the desaturases.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 4J-K.

claims.claim: TLCD2 acts independently from the desaturases.
claims.source: Firstly, we found that TLCD2 siRNA protects against the potentiated rigidifying effects of PA when the FADS2 desaturase is knocked down (Figure 4J–K; Figure 4—figure supplement 3M), just as the fld-1 mutation suppressed the effects of the fat-2 mutation in C. elegans; this also strengthens the conclusion that TLCD2 acts independently from the desaturases.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the ability of TLCD2 knockdown to suppress effects even when desaturases are knocked down.

claims.claim: TLCD2 knockdown suppresses membrane rigidification in HEK293 cells where AdipoR2 had been knocked down.
claims.source: We also found that TLCD2 knockdown suppresses membrane rigidification in HEK293 cells where AdipoR2 had been knocked down, which by itself increases the sensitivity to the effect of PA on membrane rigidification (Devkota et al., 2017) (Figure 5A–B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: AdipoR2 knockdown increases the sensitivity to the effect of PA on membrane rigidification.
claims.source: We also found that TLCD2 knockdown suppresses membrane rigidification in HEK293 cells where AdipoR2 had been knocked down, which by itself increases the sensitivity to the effect of PA on membrane rigidification (Devkota et al., 2017) (Figure 5A–B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Devkota et al., 2017.

claims.claim: TLCD2 knockdown causes a strong increase in the levels of EPA in PCs.
claims.source: As noted earlier, TLCD2 knockdown causes a strong increase in the levels of EPA in PCs (Figure 4C), which is a potent fluidizing LCPUFA: 5 μM are sufficient to completely protect AdipoR2 knockdown cells from the rigidifying effects of 200 μM PA (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: 5 μM EPA is sufficient to completely protect AdipoR2 knockdown cells from the rigidifying effects of 200 μM PA.
claims.source: As noted earlier, TLCD2 knockdown causes a strong increase in the levels of EPA in PCs (Figure 4C), which is a potent fluidizing LCPUFA: 5 μM are sufficient to completely protect AdipoR2 knockdown cells from the rigidifying effects of 200 μM PA (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by FRAP measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: TLCD1 and TLCD2 siRNA improved the UFA content of PCs and PEs in AdipoR2 knockdown cells treated with 200 μM PA.
claims.source: TLCD2 knockdown also suppresses the composition defect in HEK293 cells where AdipoR2 had been knocked down: TLCD1 and TLCD2 siRNA both improved the UFA content of PCs and PEs in AdipoR2 knockdown cells treated with 200 μM PA (Figure 5D–E), and also normalized ceramide levels in these cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 5D-E.

claims.claim: TLCD1 and TLCD2 siRNA normalized ceramide levels in AdipoR2 knockdown cells treated with PA.
claims.source: TLCD2 knockdown also suppresses the composition defect in HEK293 cells where AdipoR2 had been knocked down: TLCD1 and TLCD2 siRNA both improved the UFA content of PCs and PEs in AdipoR2 knockdown cells treated with 200 μM PA (Figure 5D–E), and also normalized ceramide levels in these cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by lipidomic analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-E.

claims.claim: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 are distantly related to the ER-localized ceramide synthases and translocation associated membrane proteins.
claims.source: Structurally, the FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 proteins are characterized by the presence of a TLC domain and are therefore distantly related to the ER-localized ceramide synthases (human CERS1-6) and to the translocation associated membrane proteins (human TRAM1, TRAM2 and TRAM1L1) involved in membrane protein synthesis in the rough ER (Pewzner-Jung et al., 2006; Winter and Ponting, 2002).
claims.evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and supported by citations.

claims.claim: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 are localized to the plasma membrane rather than in the ER.
claims.source: In contrast to the CERSs and TRAMs, FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 are localized to the plasma membrane rather than in the ER (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 4) (Papanayotou et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 are neither ceramide synthases nor translocation associated proteins.
claims.source: This, and the fact that they lack critical motifs, indicate that FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 are neither ceramide synthases nor translocation associated proteins.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from their localization and lack of critical motifs.

claims.claim: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 act at the level of the plasma membrane by limiting the amounts of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids.
claims.source: Instead, their localization and effect on PUFA content in membrane phospholipids suggest that they act at the level of the plasma membrane by limiting the amounts of LCPUFA-containing phospholipids.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from their localization and effects on lipid composition.

claims.claim: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 may influence substrate selection by phospholipases or lysophospholipid acyltransferases.
claims.source: It is possible, for example, that FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 influence substrate selection by phospholipases or lysophospholipid acyltransferases, that is regulating the Lands cycle through which phospholipids are actively remodelled by fatty acid exchange and hence effectively influence membrane composition and properties (Shindou et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of action, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The plasma membrane localisation of FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 makes a direct control of lysophospholipid acyltransferases rather unlikely.
claims.source: Note however that the plasma membrane localisation of FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 makes a direct control of lysophospholipid acyltransferases, which are believed to localize in internal membranes, notably the ER, rather unlikely.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the different subcellular localizations.

claims.claim: LCPUFAs can serve as precursors for many signalling lipids.
claims.source: The type of LCPUFAs that are elevated in the C. elegans fld-1 mutant and in HEK293 treated with siRNA against TLCD1/2 could have other effects besides influencing membrane fluidity. In particular LCPUFAs can serve as precursors for many signalling lipids (Funk, 2001; Watts, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Funk, 2001 and Watts, 2016.

claims.claim: fld-1 has its primary effects on membrane fluidity.
claims.source: That fld-1 has its primary effects on membrane fluidity is however supported by several lines of evidence, much of which hinges on the fact that fld-1 mutants act as paqr-2 and iglr-2 suppressors.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including genetic interactions and FRAP measurements.

claims.claim: The paqr-2 and iglr-2 mutants have membrane fluidity defects.
claims.source: This is important because the paqr-2 and iglr-2 mutants clearly have membrane fluidity defects since: a) They are sensitive to membrane-rigidifying conditions (cold or exogenous SFAs); b) Their mutant phenotypes are suppressed by other mutations that promote an increase in fluidizing UFAs, by exogenous UFAs or by fluidizing amounts of mild detergents (NP-40 or Triton X-100); c) The paqr-2 and iglr-2 mutants have an excess of membrane-rigidifying SFA-containing phospholipids; and d) The paqr-2 and iglr-2 phenotypes are closely associated with reduced membrane fluidity measured in vivo using FRAP under numerous different experimental conditions or genotypes (Devkota et al., 2017; Svensk et al., 2016a; Svensk et al., 2013; Svensson et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence and citations to previous work.

claims.claim: The effect of TLCD1/2 on plasma membrane composition likely explains the published observations that TLCD1 facilitates the activity of calcium channels that are essential during neural plate development.
claims.source: The effect of TLCD1/2 on plasma membrane composition likely explains the published observations that TLCD1 facilitates the activity of calcium channels that are essential during neural plate development (Papanayotou et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is an inference connecting the current findings to previous observations, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Membrane composition can have strong effects on insulin secretion by beta cells, glucose transport, endocytosis, regulation of metabolic rate, platelet aggregation and TRPV channel activity.
claims.source: Indeed, membrane composition can have strong effects on a variety of processes including insulin secretion by beta cells (MacDonald et al., 2015), glucose transport (Ginsberg et al., 1982), endocytosis (Krischer et al., 1993; Illinger et al., 1991), regulation of metabolic rate (Hulbert and Else, 2000), platelet aggregation (Winocour et al., 1990) and TRPV channel activity (Caires et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claims.claim: PUFAs are readily peroxidized.
claims.source: Conversely, given the chemical instability of PUFAs, which are readily peroxidized (Gaschler and Stockwell, 2017; Ayala et al., 2014; Kelley et al., 2014; Catalá, 2013), it seems natural for cells to have mechanisms that limit their levels.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: It seems natural for cells to have mechanisms that limit PUFA levels.
claims.source: Conversely, given the chemical instability of PUFAs, which are readily peroxidized (Gaschler and Stockwell, 2017; Ayala et al., 2014; Kelley et al., 2014; Catalá, 2013), it seems natural for cells to have mechanisms that limit their levels.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the chemical instability of PUFAs.

claims.claim: The C. elegans fld-1 mutant exhibits an enhanced oxidative stress response when challenged with LA.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that the C. elegans fld-1 mutant exhibits an enhanced oxidative stress response when challenged with the LCPUFA LA (Figure 1—figure supplement 6J–L), which indicates a function for fld-1 in preventing such PUFA-derived oxidative stress.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by gst-4::GFP reporter measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6J-L.

claims.claim: fld-1 has a function in preventing PUFA-derived oxidative stress.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that the C. elegans fld-1 mutant exhibits an enhanced oxidative stress response when challenged with the LCPUFA LA (Figure 1—figure supplement 6J–L), which indicates a function for fld-1 in preventing such PUFA-derived oxidative stress.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the enhanced oxidative stress response in the mutant.

claims.claim: The ubiquitous plasma membrane expression of C. elegans fld-1 suggests that it functions in most cells.
claims.source: The ubiquitous plasma membrane expression of C. elegans fld-1 suggests that it functions in most cells, though it is not required under non-challenging conditions given the relative health of the mutant.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the expression pattern and lack of obvious phenotypes in the single mutant.

claims.claim: fld-1 is not required under non-challenging conditions.
claims.source: The ubiquitous plasma membrane expression of C. elegans fld-1 suggests that it functions in most cells, though it is not required under non-challenging conditions given the relative health of the mutant.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of obvious phenotypes in the single mutant under normal conditions.

claims.claim: A function of paqr-2 and iglr-2 in C. elegans is to prevent SFA lipotoxicity.
claims.source: The present work further establishes that a function of paqr-2 and iglr-2 in C. elegans is to prevent SFA lipotoxicity, and specifically to prevent membrane rigidification by SFAs, and further suggests that they may act via two separate pathways: 1) Upregulation of desaturases to promote membrane fluidity; and 2) Inhibition of fld-1 directly or of a fld-1-regulated pathway.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the current work and previous studies.

claims.claim: paqr-2 and iglr-2 may act via two separate pathways: upregulation of desaturases and inhibition of fld-1 or a fld-1-regulated pathway.
claims.source: The present work further establishes that a function of paqr-2 and iglr-2 in C. elegans is to prevent SFA lipotoxicity, and specifically to prevent membrane rigidification by SFAs, and further suggests that they may act via two separate pathways: 1) Upregulation of desaturases to promote membrane fluidity; and 2) Inhibition of fld-1 directly or of a fld-1-regulated pathway.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the existence of two classes of paqr-2 suppressors.

claims.claim: There are two classes of paqr-2 suppressors: mutations that activate desaturases and loss-of-function mutations in fld-1.
claims.source: This conclusion is supported by the existence of two classes of paqr-2 suppressors: mutations that activate desaturases (e.g. gof mutations in nhr-49 or mdt-15, and lof mutations in sams-1, cept-1, pcyt-1, ech-7 or hacd-1) (Svensk et al., 2013) and loss-of-function mutations in fld-1, which does not act by upregulating desaturases though it depends on their activity (present work).
claims.evidence: This is based on the genetic screen results and characterization of suppressors.

claims.claim: paqr-2 may influence fld-1 activity.
claims.source: The suggestion that paqr-2 may influence fld-1 activity is raised only as a possibility consistent with the observed genetic interactions; we have at present no biochemical evidence that these proteins interact with each other nor do we know of a mechanism by which paqr-2 could regulate fld-1.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on genetic interactions, with explicit acknowledgment of lack of biochemical evidence.

claims.claim: Inhibitors of TLCD1/2 may have therapeutic potential in instances of lipotoxicity and excess membrane rigidity.
claims.source: We propose that inhibitors of TLCD1/2 may have therapeutic potential in instances of lipotoxicity and excess membrane rigidity, which is a feature of the diabetic condition (Pilon, 2016; Perona, 2017), or in instances of mutations in AdipoR1 that cause retina defects (Zhang et al., 2016; Rice et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a proposal for therapeutic application based on the findings, supported by citations.

claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Pilon, 2016 and Perona, 2017.

claims.claim: Inhibition of the mammalian TLCD1/2 homologs may be well tolerated.
claims.source: Encouragingly, we found that the fld-1 C. elegans single mutant has no obvious phenotype, which suggests that inhibition of the mammalian homologs may be well tolerated.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of obvious phenotypes in the C. elegans fld-1 mutant.

results.result: A forward genetic screen in C. elegans identified eight loss-of-function alleles of the novel gene fld-1, which encodes a homolog of human TLCD1/2 proteins. These mutations suppress saturated fatty acid toxicity in sensitized genetic backgrounds (paqr-2, iglr-2 mutants).
results.evaluation: The genetic screen methodology is clearly described (C13), with eight fld-1 alleles isolated from 15 suppressors (C2, C14). Loss-of-function nature is confirmed by rescue experiments (C16, C17) and Western blot showing protein absence (C18). The homology to TLCD1/2 is supported by sequence analysis (C3). The high recovery rate of fld-1 alleles provides strong evidence for its role in SFA tolerance.

results.result: FLD-1 is localized to the plasma membrane and is ubiquitously expressed throughout C. elegans development. The protein can function in multiple tissues including hypodermis and intestine to suppress paqr-2 mutant phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Plasma membrane localization is demonstrated by confocal imaging of functional GFP-tagged FLD-1 (C4, C23, C24). Tissue-specific rescue experiments show function in hypodermis and intestine (C25), supporting multi-tissue activity (C26). The functional reporter provides strong evidence for both localization and expression pattern.

results.result: Single fld-1 mutants show no obvious phenotypes under normal conditions but exhibit increased oxidative stress response when challenged with linoleic acid. All five tested alleles show similar suppression effects, indicating they are likely null alleles.
results.evaluation: Comprehensive phenotypic characterization shows no defects in multiple traits under normal conditions (C28). The specific oxidative stress phenotype with LA treatment (C29) is well-documented with imaging. The similar suppression by all five alleles (C31, C32) provides strong evidence for null status, though this is an inference rather than direct molecular proof.

results.result: fld-1 mutations suppress phenotypes of both paqr-2 and iglr-2 single and double mutants. Related genes Y48G8AL.13 and F41H10.5 show partial functional redundancy with fld-1.
results.evaluation: Genetic interaction data clearly show fld-1 suppression of iglr-2 phenotypes (C33), consistent with the known mutual dependence of paqr-2 and iglr-2 (C34). The partial suppression by related genes (C36) supports limited redundancy (C37), though the lack of glucose intolerance suppression (C35) suggests functional divergence.

results.result: fld-1 acts in a pathway separate from desaturase-activating mutations (mdt-15, cept-1, hacd-1) but requires desaturase activity for its suppression effects. fld-1 mutations restore membrane fluidity without upregulating desaturase expression.
results.evaluation: The additive genetic interactions (C38) and lack of fat-7::GFP upregulation (C42) strongly support a separate pathway (C39). FRAP measurements confirm fluidity restoration (C41). The requirement for desaturase activity shown by RNAi experiments (C43, C44) is compelling. However, the mechanism by which fld-1 depends on desaturases without regulating their expression remains unclear.

results.result: Lipidomic analysis shows that fld-1 and mdt-15 mutations correct the excess SFAs and reduced LCPUFAs in paqr-2 mutant phosphatidylethanolamines, with full correction when combined. These mutations do not cause excess membrane fluidity.
results.evaluation: The lipidomic data clearly demonstrate the lipid composition defects in paqr-2 mutants and their correction by fld-1 and mdt-15 mutations (C47, C48). The specificity for LCPUFAs over MUFAs (C49) is well-documented. FRAP data showing no excess fluidity (C51) support a regulatory mechanism preventing over-fluidization (C52), though this mechanism is not identified.

results.result: fld-1 mutations suppress the growth defect of fat-2 mutants and enable accumulation of exogenously provided EPA in paqr-2 mutants, demonstrating that LCPUFA synthesis is not required for fld-1's effects on LCPUFA-containing phospholipid levels.
results.evaluation: The genetic suppression of fat-2 by fld-1 (C53) and EPA accumulation experiments (C55) provide strong evidence that fld-1 affects LCPUFA incorporation rather than synthesis (C56). The interpretation that fld-1 increases production or decreases turnover of LCPUFA-phospholipids (C54) is reasonable but remains mechanistically unresolved at this stage.

results.result: Human TLCD1 and TLCD2 are expressed in multiple tissues and their knockdown in HEK293 cells has minimal effects under normal conditions but protects against palmitic acid-induced membrane rigidification and apoptosis.
results.evaluation: Expression data from mouse tissues (C57, C58) establish tissue distribution. FRAP measurements clearly demonstrate protection against PA-induced rigidification (C60), and apoptosis assays confirm cytoprotection (C61). The minimal effects under normal conditions (C59) parallel the C. elegans findings, supporting functional conservation.

results.result: TLCD1/2 knockdown does not affect fatty acid uptake, TAG storage, lipid sequestration, or desaturase expression. SCD expression is actually downregulated in knockdown cells.
results.evaluation: Multiple complementary assays rule out various mechanisms: PA uptake (C62), TAG content (C63, C64), Nile red staining (C65), and qPCR for desaturases (C67). The downregulation of SCD (C68) is interesting and well-documented. These negative results effectively narrow the possible mechanisms of TLCD1/2 action.

results.result: TLCD1/2 knockdown causes marked increases in specific LCPUFAs (18:2, 20:5, 22:6) in phospholipids. Exogenous EPA accumulates in knockdown cells without affecting TAG storage. Very low concentrations of LCPUFAs (1 μM EPA/DHA) prevent PA-induced membrane rigidification.
results.evaluation: Lipidomic data clearly show increased LCPUFAs in specific phospholipid classes (C69, C70). EPA supplementation experiments demonstrate independence from de novo synthesis (C71, C72) and lack of effect on TAG storage (C73). The potency of LCPUFAs in preventing rigidification (C74, C75) is well-demonstrated by FRAP and supported by literature.

results.result: Pulse-chase experiments with 13C-labeled linoleic acid show that TLCD1/2 knockdown increases LA incorporation into phospholipids within 6-24 hours but does not affect turnover during the chase period, indicating that TLCD1/2 limit LCPUFA incorporation rather than promote turnover.
results.evaluation: The isotope labeling experiments provide direct mechanistic evidence. Increased incorporation during the pulse (C76, C77) combined with no change during chase (C78) strongly support the conclusion that TLCD1/2 limit formation rather than promote turnover (C79). This is a key mechanistic finding, though only one isotope labeling experiment was performed.

results.result: TLCD2 knockdown suppresses membrane rigidification in cells with FADS2 or AdipoR2 knockdown, demonstrating independence from desaturases and functional conservation with C. elegans. TLCD knockdown improves lipid composition and normalizes ceramide levels in AdipoR2 knockdown cells.
results.evaluation: The genetic interactions with FADS2 (C80) and AdipoR2 (C82) parallel the C. elegans findings and support pathway independence (C81). The potency of EPA in protecting AdipoR2 knockdown cells (C84, C85) is well-demonstrated. Lipidomic improvements in double knockdowns (C86, C87) provide strong evidence for functional conservation across species.

results.result: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 belong to the TLC domain protein family but are localized to plasma membranes rather than ER, distinguishing them from ceramide synthases and TRAM proteins. They likely act at the plasma membrane to limit LCPUFA-containing phospholipids.
results.evaluation: Sequence analysis establishes TLC domain family membership (C88). Plasma membrane localization is clearly demonstrated by imaging (C89), distinguishing these proteins from ER-localized family members. The inference that they are not ceramide synthases or TRAMs (C90) is well-supported by localization and lack of critical motifs. The proposed mechanism (C91) is a reasonable inference from the data.

results.result: FLD-1 and TLCD1/2 may regulate the Lands cycle by influencing substrate selection of phospholipases or lysophospholipid acyltransferases, though direct control of ER-localized acyltransferases is unlikely given plasma membrane localization.
results.evaluation: This is explicitly presented as speculation (C92) with appropriate caveats about the localization mismatch (C93). While the Lands cycle hypothesis is reasonable given the data, no direct evidence for interaction with specific enzymes is provided. This represents a plausible model requiring further experimental validation.

results.result: Multiple lines of evidence support that fld-1's primary effects are on membrane fluidity rather than LCPUFA signaling functions. The effects on membrane composition can explain TLCD1's previously reported role in calcium channel activity.
results.evaluation: The argument for membrane fluidity as the primary mechanism (C95) is well-supported by the comprehensive characterization of paqr-2/iglr-2 mutants (C96) and genetic interactions. The connection to calcium channel regulation (C97) provides a plausible explanation for prior observations. The broader implications for cellular processes (C98) are well-supported by literature citations.

results.result: PUFAs are chemically unstable and readily peroxidized, suggesting cells need mechanisms to limit their levels. fld-1 mutants show enhanced oxidative stress response to LA challenge, indicating a role in preventing PUFA-derived oxidative stress.
results.evaluation: The chemical instability of PUFAs is well-established by citations (C99). The inference that cells need limiting mechanisms (C100) is reasonable. The oxidative stress phenotype in fld-1 mutants (C101) is clearly demonstrated and supports a protective function (C102). This provides a rationale for why cells would limit LCPUFA levels despite their beneficial effects on fluidity.

results.result: paqr-2 and iglr-2 prevent SFA lipotoxicity through two pathways: upregulation of desaturases and inhibition of fld-1 or a fld-1-regulated pathway. The possibility of direct paqr-2 regulation of fld-1 is raised but lacks biochemical evidence.
results.evaluation: The two-pathway model (C106) is well-supported by the existence of two suppressor classes (C107) and the genetic interaction data. The function in preventing SFA lipotoxicity (C105) is clearly established. The speculation about direct paqr-2/fld-1 interaction (C108) is appropriately presented with explicit acknowledgment of the lack of biochemical evidence.

results.result: TLCD1/2 inhibitors may have therapeutic potential for lipotoxicity, diabetes-associated membrane rigidity, and AdipoR1-related retinal defects. The lack of obvious phenotypes in fld-1 mutants suggests inhibition may be well-tolerated.
results.evaluation: This is explicitly presented as a proposal for future therapeutic applications (C109). While the associations with diabetes (C110) and retinal defects (C111) are supported by citations, no actual therapeutic studies are presented. The inference about tolerability (C112) is reasonable but extrapolating from C. elegans to mammals is speculative. This represents a reasonable hypothesis requiring validation.
